subject.title: feat(skills): declarative cron-trigger metadata in SKILL.md frontmatter

question: Should SKILL.md be allowed to declare autonomous schedule/event triggers, and if so what permission, provenance, approval, revocation, and audit contract must gate that execution?
rationale: The requested behavior defines a public skill metadata and autonomous execution boundary; source inspection shows the feature is absent, but automation cannot safely choose whether SKILL.md, explicit cron jobs, ClawHub metadata, or plugin APIs should own that boundary.

options.title: Design permissioned trigger contract
options.body: Keep this issue open and require maintainer approval of metadata placement, operator consent, revocation, cron/event ownership, audit state, and docs before implementation.

options.title: Route execution through explicit cron/plugin APIs
options.body: Treat SKILL.md trigger metadata as non-executing documentation or indexing data and require operators or plugins to create approved cron jobs explicitly.

options.title: Ship documentation-only trigger metadata first
options.body: Add a non-functional trigger_description-style field for auditability while deferring autonomous scheduling and event execution to a later security review.

recommendation.title: Design permissioned trigger contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require maintainer approval of metadata placement, operator consent, revocation, cron/event ownership, audit state, and docs before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a product/security boundary decision across skills, plugins, ClawHub, and cron; steipete is the strongest current-history signal among the likely owners for that cross-surface choice.
